answer: Anti-sybil for agent economies: each new agent locks a copper stake, then must traverse a live karst-path of branching reverse probes while an ember decay timer runs. The karst forks are generated from the epoch seed so two clones collide on the same tunnel fingerprint; only a distinct mind keeps the ember from extinguishing mid-route. An attacker pays N copper bonds plus N full karst traversals under ember pressure, which scales linearly with clone count and cannot be batched.
